b1.meaning: every frame (30 / 25 fps), held-out frames out

a1-motion.meaning: current + extras by camera motion to the 5 fps frame count

a1-novel.meaning: current + extras by new content to the 5 fps count

a2-motion.meaning: 5 fps + extras by camera motion to the 10 fps count

a2-novel.meaning: 5 fps + extras by new content to the 10 fps count

G5.meaning: DA3 any-view on 5 fps keyframes, one forward per shot (production)

Gmotion.meaning: 5 fps + extras by camera motion, 10 fps view budget, one forward

G30i.meaning: every frame: interleaved chunks (all 5 fps frames + every m-th other, <= 300 views) Sim3 onto G5

G30c.meaning: every frame: consecutive 150-view chunks chained by Sim3 on shared frames' depth

p-adapt.meaning: 5 fps, and 15 fps frames only between keyframes where SAM 3 saw a person

method.timing: analysis only: t0 = models warm and the MP4 bytes in the container; cold start (boot) recorded separately and excluded. Batch, 2 x A100-SXM4-80GB per container (all seven containers, smokes included, got SXM4), no MPS (one process), cpu 16, 96 GiB, ephemeral modal run, retries 0
method.memory: nvidia-smi device-wide GiB per GPU sampled every 50 ms (fast_report.instrument.Vram); per stage and per GPU peaks; >90% (72 GiB) flagged: no flag in any run
method.sam3: SAM 3 (sam3_app pin, bf16, 80 pairs per forward; vocabulary floor 0.3, no cap, a-core's flood dedupe per frame; person/floor 0.4, top 12) run ONCE on every frame; each rate is a subset of the same per-frame masks (image mode, frames independent). Timed in nested phases; a rate's SAM 3 time = its frames x the measured GPU s/frame / 2 GPUs [M x n]
method.vocabulary: fixed per site: the Qwen3-VL v1 per-video list of runs/fb-d-harness-gaps-001 (ME340 57 words, Sam's Club 22, Walmart 18); no VLM in the loop, so no run-to-run vocabulary spread between rates
method.rates: b6x3 = a-core's object keyframes (every 3rd sharpest-of-6 keyframe: 1.67 fps at 29.97 fps, 1.39 at 25); b6 = every sharpest-of-6 keyframe (5.0 / 4.17); b3 = sharpest of each 3 (10 / 8.3); b2 = sharpest of each 2 (15 / 12.5); b1 = every frame (29.2 / 24.4 after held-out frames). Blocks aligned to frame 0 as a-core
method.geometry: DA3-GIANT-1.1 any-view 504x280, cam head, per shot (a-core's Da3.shot). G5 = production. Objects and people at every rate lift with the same geometry: G5's own depth/pose on 5 fps frames, in-between frames from G30i (G5's world), scale from G5's floor plane + assumed 1.6 m camera height
method.held_out: about 1 frame per second of the reference shot that has the delivered DA3-posed depth (ME340 22, Sam's 17, Walmart 15) is never used by any configuration. Held-out depth: each configuration's TSDF mesh ray-cast from DROID's camera moved into our frame by that configuration's own Sim3 (E1's render_depth_eval rule, 320x240 raster of the 4:3 centre), compared with the delivered DA3-posed depth; people (SAM 3 person, dilated) left out
method.objects_metrics: recall = fast_report_eval.objects3d_row (delivered named-map objects seen >= 3 times in our shot, centroid within 0.3 / 0.5 m after the G5 trajectory Sim3 to DROID); split by delivered box size (native AABB x metres_per_native, estimated); word-matched = an object within 0.5 m whose SAM 3 word matches the delivered name (fast_report_eval.same_name). small = longest extent < 0.3 m; thin/long = longest >= 0.3 m and >= 3 x the middle one; extents = the median over an object's views of that view's own lifted points' principal extents (sqrt(12 lambda)), depth-edge pixels out, metres ESTIMATED. new_vs_current = < 10% of the object's 5 cm voxels inside any current-rate object. view_centroid_spread = median distance of each view's lifted-mask centroid from the median centroid (objects with >= 3 views)
method.outlines_metric: 60 evaluation frames per video that no configuration except 'every frame' segments; reference = the every-frame run's objects' SAM 3 masks at that frame (static: < 50% on a person; >= 1200 px at 1280x720). projected = a-core's E6b 'pair' projection from the configuration's two nearest segmented frames with G30i depth/pose, people cut out; held = the last segmented frame's outline unchanged. iou_area_weighted = each reference object's best IoU with any projected region, area-weighted; object_pixels_iou = all object pixels vs all object pixels (no identity, so fragmentation differences between rates do not count)
method.people_metrics: ehs_spatial.live_people.PeopleLoop via core.people_shot on the configuration's frames; fast_report_eval.people_row (path difference on the floor vs the delivered dynamic layer's person centroids, <= 1 m match); ID switches = changes of the matched delivered person inside one of our tracks; extra tracks = our tracks beyond one per matched delivered person; rule agreement = fast_report_eval.rule_agreement ticks (0.2 s) vs our 5 fps run, and vs E3 ref10 on ME340
method.adaptive: a1 = current object frames + extra frames up to the 5 fps count; a2 = 5 fps + extra up to the 10 fps count; extras placed per keyframe interval by largest remainder in proportion to camera motion (G5 rotation + translation over median depth, degrees) or to new content (1 - share of the next keyframe's depth pixels covered by the previous keyframe's points splatted into it, G5 geometry). Gmotion = the a2-motion frame set as DA3 views. p-adapt = 5 fps plus the 15 fps frames that lie between 5 fps keyframes where SAM 3 saw a person

conclusions.note: interpretation of the numbers in 'summary' and 'sites'; three videos, one run each, so differences of ~0.02 in recall are inside run-to-run noise (not measured here)
conclusions.objects: Best rate: segment every 5 fps keyframe (a-core's OBJECT_EVERY 3 -> 1). Recall at 0.5 m vs the delivered reports, current -> 5 fps: ME340 0.589 -> 0.716, Sam's Club 0.455 -> 0.487, Walmart 0.605 -> 0.745 (mean 0.550 -> 0.649) for +22.4 / +8.9 / +7.4 s of SAM 3 on 2 A100s [M x n]. 10 fps adds +0.02 mean (0.668) for another +33.6 / +13.5 / +11.1 s; 15 fps (0.642) and every frame (0.609) fall back. More frames give many more objects (ME340 263 -> 653 -> 937 -> 1294 -> 2453): the contact sheets show real structures seen only briefly (ceiling conduits/pipes, cables, light fixtures, control panel, power tools; Walmart pallet, shopping cart, stacked boxes, shelf segments) plus fragments of already-found objects. Thin/long delivered objects gain most from rate (ME340 recall 0.2 -> 0.5 -> 0.6 -> 0.6 -> 0.7 for 10 objects), small delivered objects lose above 10 fps (ME340 1.0 -> 1.0 -> 0.96 -> 0.83 -> 0.70). Word-matched recall stays 0.10-0.14 on ME340 at every rate (vocabulary-limited) and follows position recall on Walmart (0.27 -> 0.42 at 5 fps, 0.29 at every frame).
conclusions.outlines: In-between-frame outlines improve steadily with rate: object-pixel IoU vs the every-frame masks, current -> 5 -> 10 -> 15 fps: ME340 0.70 -> 0.81 -> 0.81 -> 0.84, Sam's 0.66 -> 0.78 -> 0.82 -> 0.85, Walmart 0.37 -> 0.65 -> 0.70 -> 0.72. Projection beats holding the last keyframe on Sam's/Walmart (area-weighted IoU +0.04 to +0.08 at the current rate), ties on ME340.
conclusions.geometry: Best rate for the camera path: 5 fps. More views do not lower ATE vs DROID (ME340 G5 4.11 cm, G10 4.04, every frame one forward 4.37, interleaved 4.34; Sam's 22.2 / 19.6 / 24.7 / 23.5 cm; Walmart 18.1 / 18.4 / 20.1 / 19.4 cm; G5 / G10 / every frame all 0.9-1.3% of the path). More views fill holes: held-out coverage G5 -> G10 -> every frame: ME340 0.948 -> 0.970 -> 0.979, Sam's 0.820 -> 0.860 -> 0.876, Walmart 0.760 -> 0.834 -> 0.874, but depth agreement there does not improve (absrel ME340 0.056 -> 0.064 -> 0.075). Every frame in ONE forward is feasible for these 30 s clips (ME340 651 views 126 s, device peak 68 GiB on GPU 1; Sam's 403 views 51 s; Walmart 352 views 39 s) but is not better. Consecutive 150-view chunks chained by Sim3 are worse (ATE ME340 16.4 cm, Sam's 30.3 cm; ghosting in the renders): short chunks have too little baseline; interleaved chunks that all contain the 5 fps frames, put onto G5 by the Sim3 of those frames' depth (median fit residual 0.3-1.4% of depth, vs 0.5-4.9% for the consecutive chain), keep G5's ATE and are how in-between frames were given poses here. The motion-placed 10 fps view budget (Gmotion) gave the best ATE on ME340 (3.06 cm) and Sam's (20.7 cm) but the worst on Walmart (25.2 cm), at G10's cost (21 / 15 / 13 s DA3).
conclusions.people: Best rate: 5 fps, with 15 fps only where people are if speed matters. Path difference vs the delivered tracks (median): ME340 7.2 cm at 5 fps vs 8.3 at 10 and 15; Walmart 15.2 -> 10.9 -> 10.2 cm; Sam's Club ~64-65 cm at every rate (limited by its geometry: ATE 22 cm, scale 1.12). ID switches unchanged (ME340 0, Walmart 1, Sam's 0 at every rate); 15 fps adds one extra track per video. R3 speed verdicts agree with 5 fps on 93-99% of ticks (ME340, Walmart) and 82-84% (Sam's), with no PASS<->FAIL flip anywhere. Person-adaptive 15 fps matched uniform 15 fps on path difference and identity with 214 instead of 375 frames on Walmart (325 vs 375 Sam's, 437 vs 443 ME340).
conclusions.adaptive: For objects, adaptive does not beat uniform at equal frame count: current + motion/novelty extras to the 5 fps count gave recall 0.632/0.600 (ME340), 0.487/0.474 (Sam's), 0.694/0.694 (Walmart) vs uniform 5 fps 0.716 / 0.487 / 0.745, and lower outline IoU; 5 fps + extras to the 10 fps count tied uniform 10 fps (0.737/0.726, 0.506/0.500, 0.745/0.739 vs 0.726 / 0.513 / 0.764). For people it wins (same path difference and identity, up to 43% fewer frames). For geometry it is mixed (see Gmotion).
conclusions.cost_and_memory: SAM 3 GPU s/frame measured: person+floor 0.063-0.069, vocabulary 0.381 (57 words), 0.147 (22), 0.115 (18), dedupe 0.004-0.023. SAM 3 on 2 A100s for current / 5 / 10 / 15 / 30 fps [M x n]: ME340 11 / 34 / 67 / 101 / 196 s, Sam's 4.5 / 13 / 27 / 40 / 79 s, Walmart 3.7 / 11 / 22 / 33 / 65 s. Nested phases measured on ME340: the 50 current frames 14.1 s, +100 frames to 5 fps 24.4 s. Device peak per GPU during the SAM 3 pass 38-44 GiB (this sweep's layout: per-frame dedupe, kept masks bit-packed on the CPU, 3.3 GB for all ME340 frames). a-core's layout keeps every vocabulary mask and its logits on GPU 0: from the measured mask counts that is 5.3 / 15.8 / 31 / 47 / 91 GiB on ME340 [M x n]; a-core's GPU 0 peak was 45 GB at the current rate (runs/fb-a-core-011), which already holds the 5.3, so ~55 at 5 fps, ~71 at 10 (the 90% line), ~86 at 15 (over the card) [E]: above 5 fps a-core needs this sweep's streaming layout. segment.lift multiplies scipy's int32 component labels by the voxel count: it overflowed at 30 fps here (fixed with int64 in lift_big); a-core's copy has the same limit.
